summary: Lever-C EIG via in-distribution system-prompt channel
hypothesis: Delivering solution-space EIG (competing scenarios) through the system prompt while keeping the byte-exact native user anchor — the proven in-distribution format from exp040 — would give lever C a fair test, since exp030's regression to 0.305 may have been caused by the reframed user prompt pulling the adapter off its native training format rather than by the lever itself.
technique: The exp040 adapter is called with divergent solution-space scenarios injected into the system prompt only, while the final user prompt is kept as the exact native anchor used during adapter training — isolating the lever-C grounding from any user-prompt reframing confound.
result: Scored 0.393 on the full-30 greedy eval (2 wins / 1 tie / 17 losses vs Sonnet); rubric: atom=4, spec=3, cover=3, nat=3, nonRed=4. Coverage stayed pinned at 3 with the same modal misses verbatim as prior lever-C attempts, confirming coverage judgment is weight-locked and not promptable. A new pathology emerged: the analytical scenario block triggered FM content-moderation on 10/30 cases and overflowed the 4096-token context on 2 cases — actively worse than the champion (0.409). Hypothesis falsified; discarded.
